pr_title: sql:  add notice for Alter TYPE ADD VALUE IF NOT EXIST command
pr_body:
Fixes: #52327

Added a notice message similar to postgres if user tries to add a value in enum which already exists using IF NOT EXIST command.

> root@:26257/defaultdb> alter type color ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'black';
ALTER TYPE

> root@:26257/defaultdb> alter type color ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'black';
NOTICE: enum label "black" already exists, skipping 

However, I noticed similar behaviour in other command like ALTER TABLE command. Altering existing table with if not exist 
command doesn't shows any notice.

Release note (sql change): Show notice to user when user tries to add value which already exists in enum .

issue_context.title: sql: improve HINT when using IF NOT EXISTS and ENUMs
issue_context.body:
In PG, if you try to create an enum label that already exists it provides a NOTICE that let's you know it already exists and skipping. In CRDB we silently succeed. We should match PG:
```SQL
postgres=# alter type color_t ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'pink' AFTER 'gray';
NOTICE:  enum label "pink" already exists, skipping
ALTER TYPE
```

review_comments: Last nit -- don't also remove the comment that actually tells what the function does!
Update the comment here now to say that "AddEnumValue assumes that the type is an enum, and that the new value doesn't exist already in the enum"
updated comment, i will make sure to do such descriptive code comments in future contributions.
